chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, who said:
I heard Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) saying: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad (عليه السلام) used to say: If we were not increased, we would be exhausted.
Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Ṣafwān, from Abū al-Ḥasan, similarly.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam being quoted in the narration
key_terms.جَعْفَرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام)
key_terms.لَأَنْفَدْنَا: we would be exhausted or depleted
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: similar to it; another chain reporting the same meaning
key_terms.نَزْدَادُ: we are increased; receive continual addition

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith 'If we were not increased, we would run out' mean about the Imams’ knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Imams (عليهم السلام) are continually increased in what they possess, indicating an ongoing divine bestowal rather than a finite store that could be depleted. In Shia theological context, it points to the ever-renewed divine support and knowledge granted to the Imams (عليهم السلام).
